title: Bṛhaspati, give us that bright wealth

sandhi_exceptions.note: बृहस्पते अति: the vocative’s -e stays before a, unjoined, as the Saṃhitā and the Ṛgveda both write it.
अर्यो अर्हात्: -aḥ becomes -o and the following a is kept, the regular Vedic treatment inside a pāda.
शवसा ऋतप्रजात: final -ā before ṛ is left unjoined, as in the Ṛgveda.

words.context: Sāyaṇa: the lord of the brahman, the priest of the gods

words.role: opens the relative clause, answered by tat
qualifies the wealth, or how it shines

words.meaning: O you born of the order (of truth)

sandhi.rule: -t before a vowel becomes -d; -aḥ before a becomes -o

samasa.meaning: born of ṛta, the cosmic order and truth

morphology.note: subjunctive with the a-augment (let), ‘may he deserve’; Sāyaṇa so explains it.

translation.literal: Bṛhaspati, that which the noble one may deserve above [others], which shines out brilliantly and effectively among men, which may shine with strength, O born of ṛta — that bright wealth place in us.
translation.readable: Bṛhaspati, born of the sacred order: the wealth that a noble man most deserves, that shines with splendour and power among men, that blazes with strength — that bright wealth, give it to us.

meaning: A prayer to Bṛhaspati, the lord of sacred speech, the gods’ priest (RV 2.23.15; TS 1.8.22.2). He is asked to place in the worshippers the wealth that a noble man deserves above others, that shines among men and blazes with strength. Sāyaṇa, on the Ṛgveda, takes that wealth to be the radiance of sacred knowledge, brahmavarcasa, and quotes a Brāhmaṇa that uses the verse for one who wants that radiance; Bhaṭṭa Bhāskara, on the Saṃhitā, takes it as wealth a lord rightly deserves. The verse names Bṛhaspati in its first word.
in_the_rite: The mantra of Bṛhaspati (Jupiter), first of the three in his step of the Navagraha sūktam (witness S): the verse addresses Bṛhaspati by name. Its use for a graha belongs to the later gṛhya tradition.

commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: Sāyaṇa, on the Ṛgveda, addresses Bṛhaspati as «ऋतप्रजात सत्येनोत्पन्न» and reads the wealth as the radiance of sacred knowledge; he cites a Brāhmaṇa that uses the verse for one who is «ब्रह्मवर्चसकामो», desirous of that radiance.

commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: Bhaṭṭa Bhāskara, on the Saṃhitā: the noble one is «स्वामी विद्वान्राजा वा», a lord, a learned man or a king; the wealth shines «शवसा बलेन अन्नेन वा», with strength or with food; and Bṛhaspati is «सत्य-प्रभव», sprung from truth.

notes.label: linguistic
notes.text: A triṣṭubh. The Saṃhitā and the Ṛgveda keep the hiatus at three places (बृहस्पते अति, अर्यो अर्हात्, शवसा ऋत-), declared above.
